items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: >> [(prose)] All those youngsters and even the crippled characters -- there was a guy called "Crip". He had one leg. He would be the leader sometimes, leading the second line on his peg leg.

ctx.x: the graveyard, and they buried most of the people in New Orleans in vaults, like in tombs, you know, because it's like swampland still, you know. They can't bury so deep because it's muddy and the soft mud and all that. So they make -- they called vaults, you know, and they play all this sad music going to the grave and they stand around when they put the character -- whoever died -- in the vault -- tomb, they call it, and seal him up. And the band turned around and come out and they say, "Ta-tat," and then the…

All those youngsters and even the crippled characters -- there was a guy called "Crip". He had one leg. He would be the leader sometimes, leading the second line on his peg leg. So it was a lot of fun.

I saw in -- I think it was what? -- Leonard says that you didn't want to be a musician but your family wanted you to be. Was that -- in Leonard's book? And then I read in Chilton that you worked with a photo engraver before becoming a musician?
